songInfo.title: 17 (I Wish I Was)
songInfo.genre: Australian Pub Rock / New Wave Rock

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: D Mixolydian energetic pub rock combining syncopated new-wave chord stabs with driving I - ♭VII - IV - V cadence hooks

scalesUsed.notes: D - E - F# - G - A - B - C
scalesUsed.application: Shapes the signature bouncing rhythm riff with the flattened 7th degree (C major chord) providing raw rock swagger
Supplies the melodic fill phrasing and soaring opening hooks that punctuate the vocal lines
Drives the searing, blues-infused guitar solo break with aggressive unison bends and fast vibrato

mainProgression.description: An infectious, fast-bouncing Australian pub-rock engine that balances melodic pop hooks with aggressive hard-rock punch

sectionProgressions.description: Bouncing, syncopated power chord riff opening establishing the tight 146 BPM danceable rock pulse
Tight palm-muted open D pedal chug interspersed with sharp, punchy off-beat chord stabs
Explosive open chord singalong chorus carrying the unforgettable nostalgic pub anthem hook
Uncompromising hard-driving rhythm bed supporting soaring melodic and blues-scale lead work

harmonicFunction: D (Tonic I): Tonal home base anchored by a driving open 4th-string pedal pulse
C (Subtonic ♭VII): Injects the vital Mixolydian bite that removes classical leading-tone stiffness
G (Subdominant IV): Uplifting chord transition that bridges the verse into the melodic turnaround
A (Dominant V): The classic dominant motor that drives the harmony decisively back into the tonic D

techniques.name: Syncopated Upbeat Chord Stabbing
techniques.description: Punching accents precisely on the upbeats ('and') while maintaining a steady downbeat pedal pulse

notes: Keep the right hand moving in a continuous 16th-note rhythm pattern
Mute strings with the left fretting hand immediately after striking the chord to create staccato punch
Anchor the low open D string between accents to maintain harmonic stability

techniques.name: High-Fret Pentatonic Bending
techniques.description: Executing expressive whole-step bends and unison bends across the 10th through 15th frets with wide vibrato

notes: Reinforce the bending finger with the index and middle fingers behind it
Target the true pitch with pinpoint intonation before applying finger vibrato
Damp unused lower strings with the picking hand palm to eliminate unwanted stage noise

sections.name: Syncopated Bouncing Intro
sections.description: The high-energy guitar intro that instantly fills pub dance floors across Australia, driven by bouncy power chord stabs
notes: Keep the open D string chugging with light palm muting
Snap sharply into the 3rd fret C5 and G5 power chords
Accentuate the A5 power chord on beat 4 of the turnaround measure

sections.name: Tight New-Wave Pub Verse
sections.description: Rhythm section lays down a tight, percussive groove supporting Brian Nichol's dynamic vocal storytelling
notes: Apply even palm muting to the four repeated D5 downstrokes
Unmute cleanly on the syncopated C5 and G5 chord stabs
Keep the tempo rock-steady at 146 BPM without rushing the stabs

sections.name: Euphoric Pub-Rock Chorus
sections.description: The massive, soaring chorus ringing out with full-voiced open D, C, G, and A chords and infectious crowd vocal hooks
notes: Strike the open D chord with a full downward strum across the top four strings
Use a full C major cowboy chord or C add9 for extra chime
Let the ringing G and A major chords sustain with warm tube breakup

sections.name: Searing Pentatonic Solo
sections.description: Stephen 'Fess' Parker's explosive guitar solo cutting through the mix with high-register bends, fast hammer-ons, and crying vibrato
notes: Target the 10th-fret D root on the high E string to kick off the lead
Execute an aggressive whole-step bend at the 13th fret of the B string
Climb into the upper register at the 15th and 17th frets for the solo climax

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Custom or Fender Stratocaster with bridge humbucker
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker delivering sharp, cutting treble and dense midrange punch

amp.recommended: Marshall JMP 2203 100W Master Volume into 4x12 cabinet with Celestion G12-65 speakers

effects.distortion: Natural British valve overdrive pushed with an MXR Distortion+ or Boss SD-1
effects.reverb: Subtle studio plate reverb to give the guitars spatial width
effects.other: Boss CE-2 chorus pedal for a subtle late-70s / early-80s shimmer on the verse rhythm tracks

beginner.title: Chords & Basic Progression
steps: Learn the open D, C, G, and A major chord fingerings
Practice shifting cleanly between D, C, G, and A at 110 BPM
Master the basic eighth-note strumming pattern with a metronome

intermediate.title: Syncopated Stabbing & Palm Muting
steps: Develop the tight palm-muted verse chug at 146 BPM
Coordinate the off-beat chord stabs with crisp left-hand muting
Transition seamlessly from palm-muted verse into wide-open chorus

advanced.title: Full Lead Solo & Live Swagger
steps: Learn the complete guitar solo in D Minor Pentatonic
Master the 13th-fret and 15th-fret whole-step bends with accurate pitch
Capture the authentic high-energy Australian pub rock stage dynamic

commonMistakes: Rushing the off-beat C5 and G5 chord stabs during the verse
Letting open strings ring erratically when jumping between D and C chords
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Right-hand alternate picking and palm-muting warm-up
10 mins: Syncopated chord stab rhythm drill with a metronome at 125 BPM
10 mins: D Minor Pentatonic solo bending practice targeting pitch accuracy at the 13th and 15th frets
5 mins: Full track playthrough locking into the 146 BPM live groove
focusAreas: Crisp, percussive silence between syncopated chord stabs
Even dynamic volume across all four open chorus chords
Sustained, singing finger vibrato on the solo resolution notes
metronomeWork: Start at 115 BPM to lock in the syncopated rhythm placements
Increase tempo to 130 BPM, focusing on keeping the left-hand muting razor-sharp
Perform at full 146 BPM, ensuring zero forearm tension during the driving verse chugs
